title: The Woman's Trick Against Her Husband

keywords: the woman's trick against her husband
full_text:
In the city of Basra lived an affluent linen-draper named Abu Bakr whose excessive jealousy was the talk of the entire quarter. Though his wife was a model of virtue, modesty, and domestic care, Abu Bakr locked the courtyard gates with three heavy bolts whenever he left for the market, refusing to allow even the old water-carrier or the bread-woman to enter.

Weary of being treated like a prisoner, the witty wife resolved to cure his ridiculous jealousy through an innocent comedy.

One morning, having observed that Abu Bakr was returning home early from the bazaar, she purchased a large, empty cedar shipping crate from a passing carpenter. She placed the crate in the center of the courtyard, left the lid half-open, and threw an old pair of men’s yellow slippers beside it on the tiles.

When Abu Bakr unlocked the three bolts and stepped into the courtyard, his eyes fell upon the yellow slippers. He turned purple with rage: 'Whose slippers are these? Who is hiding in my house?'

His wife ran out from the kitchen, feigning extreme panic, threw her arms across the crate, and cried: 'O husband, do not open that chest! By all that is sacred, do not look inside!'

Blinded by fury, Abu Bakr pushed her aside, shouting: 'Aha! The traitor is concealed within! I shall lock the crate, carry it directly to the Chief Justice, and have you both banished from Basra!'

He slammed down the heavy lid, padlocked it with an iron chain, hoisted the heavy wooden crate upon his back, and staggered through the crowded streets beneath the blazing sun!

A crowd of neighbors, merchants, and schoolboys followed the puffing linen-draper as he marched up to the tribunal of the Chief Judge.

'Justice, O Judge!' gasped Abu Bakr, dropping the crate with a crash before the bench. 'Open this crate and behold the deceiver who has violated my domestic honor!'

The judge ordered the locksmiths to break the chain. The lid was thrown open. The entire courtroom leaned forward with breathless suspense—only to find the crate completely empty, save for a large round turnip and a folded parchment inscribed with a verse:

'He who locks out the sun in fear of shadows
Will carry a turnip to court on his own shoulders!'

The courtroom erupted into roaring laughter. The judge laughed until tears rolled down his cheeks, reprimanded Abu Bakr for his foolish suspicion, and sent him home to beg his wife’s pardon, having cured his jealousy forever.
moral: Unreasonable jealousy and suspicion make a man a fool, easily cured by clever good humor.
